scope: Deployer-facing processing, retention, erasure, and transfer inventory for the svelte-adapter-uws ecosystem.

packages.name: svelte-adapter-uws
packages.role: HTTP/WebSocket runtime, browser transport client, in-process plugins, and telemetry boundary

packages.name: svelte-realtime
packages.role: Realtime RPC/state framework, browser offline queue, durable-work seams, and erasure coordinator

packages.name: svelte-adapter-uws-extensions
packages.role: Redis and Postgres persistence, coordination, replay, dead-letter, alarm, job, and task stores

responsibilityModel.ecosystem: Supplies processing primitives and documented deletion controls; it is not a hosted processor and does not select a lawful basis or retention period for the deployment.
responsibilityModel.deployer: Acts as controller or processor according to its service, configures data minimisation and retention, inventories infrastructure vendors, services data-subject requests, and verifies deletion across every configured store and sink.
responsibilityModel.infrastructureProvider: May be a processor or subprocessor when Redis, Postgres, log, metric, trace, browser storage, backup, or hosting services receive personal data. The deployer must identify the provider and transfer mechanism.

erasureBoundary.covered: Known in-process user-keyed realtime stores and a configured durable store exposing purgeUser(tenantId, userId, cascade).
erasureBoundary.notCovered: Application databases, browser sessionStorage/IndexedDB, logs, metrics, traces, backups, unregistered custom stores, records without a user mapping, and adapter-only in-process stores.
erasureBoundary.completionRule: Do not report erasure complete until the application has enumerated this manifest, run every applicable ecosystem and host deletion action, handled failures, and recorded evidence from external stores, sinks, replicas, and backups.

activities.purpose: Serve SvelteKit HTTP requests and authenticated/authorized WebSocket traffic.
activities.storage: Adapter request/connection objects and application handlers; the adapter does not durably persist the request or message body.

defaultRetention.limit: Released after request completion, WebSocket close, or process termination; application code and sinks may copy it elsewhere.

erasure.action: Delete any copies made by application handlers, proxies, logs, traces, or downstream services.
erasure.limitations: Closing a connection removes live adapter state but does not erase copied or exported records.

hostActions: Document the lawful basis and recipient for request and message data.
Classify proxy, application, and observability copies separately.
activities.transfer: Depends on deployment region, hosting, proxy, and downstream recipients.

activities.purpose: Resume a previous WebSocket session after reconnecting.

defaultRetention.limit: Browser-defined sessionStorage lifetime; the client overwrites the identifier but does not expose an ecosystem-wide remote deletion control.

erasure.action: Remove the sessionStorage key in the browser or instruct the user to clear site data/close the tab as appropriate.
erasure.limitations: live.forget does not execute in each browser and cannot clear sessionStorage.

hostActions: Disclose browser storage where required.
Provide a sign-out/site-data path if the identifier is linked to an account.
activities.transfer: No third-party transfer by the storage primitive; network resume sends the identifier to the configured deployment.

activities.purpose: Replay recent topic events after a transient subscriber gap.
subjects: application-defined users and entities represented in payloads
activities.storage: Per-process memory, bounded by 100 topics and 1000 entries per topic by default.

defaultRetention.policy: capacity and process lifetime; no time TTL
defaultRetention.limit: Least-recently-used topic and oldest-entry eviction, explicit clear/clearTopic, or process termination.

erasure.action: Call clearTopic for every affected topic, or clear the store/restart the process when selective mapping is unavailable.
erasure.limitations: The adapter replay store has no built-in user index and is not included in live.forget.

hostActions: Avoid personal data in replay payloads where possible.
Define a user-to-topic erasure mapping or choose a durable store with forgetUserId.
activities.transfer: None unless payloads are relayed or exported by application configuration.

activities.purpose: Hold application session values and deduplication identifiers in one process.
activities.storage: Per-process memory; both APIs require a positive deployer-selected TTL and default to 10000 entries.

defaultRetention.limit: Sliding TTL for sessions, claim-window TTL for deduplication, capacity eviction, explicit delete/clear, or process termination.

erasure.action: Delete the known token/id or clear the store; rotate credentials if the token may have escaped.
erasure.limitations: These adapter stores are not registered with live.forget and user lookup is application-owned.

hostActions: Set TTLs from the declared purpose, not only capacity needs.
Maintain the user-to-token mapping needed for selective erasure.
activities.transfer: In-process unless application code exports values.

activities.purpose: Queue RPC mutations while disconnected and replay them after reconnecting.
activities.storage: Browser memory by default; opt-in offline.persist=true uses IndexedDB. maxQueue defaults to 100, maxAge defaults to 0 (no age expiry), and persistKey defaults to default.

defaultRetention.policy: until replay/settlement, eviction, explicit browser-store deletion, or browser storage removal; no default age limit
defaultRetention.limit: Capacity bounds count but does not bound age. A positive maxAge must be configured for time-bounded retention.

erasure.action: Clear the account-specific offline-store prefix on sign-out/erasure and reject or discard queued mutations for the forgotten identity.
erasure.limitations: live.forget runs on the server and does not clear IndexedDB in disconnected browsers; the default persistKey is not user-partitioned.

hostActions: Use an account-specific persistKey.
Set a positive maxAge.
Clear old-user data before switching accounts on a shared browser.
activities.transfer: Stored locally until replay sends the payload to the configured server.

data: optionally full arguments, results, and stream values
activities.storage: Browser/process memory in bounded development-tool collections; payload capture is off by default.

defaultRetention.policy: development session and bounded collection lifetime
defaultRetention.limit: Clear action, collection replacement, disabling unsafeCapturePayloads (which purges captured payload values), reload, or process termination.

erasure.action: Disable unsafeCapturePayloads and clear the development event collection/reload the page.
erasure.limitations: Screenshots, copied values, browser extensions, and external developer tooling are outside the purge boundary.

hostActions: Do not enable payload capture against production personal data.
Use synthetic or minimised development fixtures.
activities.transfer: Depends on browser, remote debugging, screen sharing, and developer tooling configuration.

activities.purpose: Coordinate presence, rate limits, idempotency, reactive cohorts, CRDT replicas, push subscriptions, smooth state, and dead-letter handling.
activities.storage: Process memory with surface-specific TTL/capacity/lifecycle rules; in-memory idempotency defaults to 48 hours and dead letters default to 1000 records with no TTL.

defaultRetention.policy: mixed surface-specific lifecycle; some stores have no time default
defaultRetention.limit: live.forget covers its registered user-keyed surface, but CRDT durable persistence, unmapped dead letters, and other application-owned copies require additional action.

erasure.action: Authenticate the caller, invoke live.forget, treat FORGET_STORE_FAILED as incomplete erasure, and run every application/browser/sink deletion leg.
erasure.limitations: Coverage depends on configured durable purgeUser support and identity extractors; it is not a universal data-discovery mechanism.

hostActions: Register the durable forget store and identity extractors.
Test failure and retry behavior.
Inventory custom stores outside the descriptor table.
activities.transfer: Depends on configured extension stores, push providers, webhook recipients, and application services.

activities.purpose: Persist topic events for reconnect replay across processes and restarts.
subjects: users and entities represented in topics or payloads
activities.storage: Redis or Postgres. Both replay stores default to 1000 entries per topic and ttl=0 (no expiry).

defaultRetention.policy: capacity-bounded but indefinite by time unless ttl is configured
defaultRetention.limit: Oldest-entry eviction, configured positive TTL, clearTopic/clear, purgeUser with forgetUserId, or infrastructure deletion.

erasure.action: Configure forgetUserId, connect the store to live.forget, and verify purgeUser removed matching rows/events from every instance/store.
erasure.limitations: Without forgetUserId, purgeUser is a no-op; capacity eviction is not an erasure deadline.

hostActions: Set a positive TTL from the declared replay window.
Keep payloads minimal and make user mapping deterministic.
Address replicas and backups.
activities.transfer: Redis/Postgres and their hosting, replication, backup, and support regions may be subprocessors/transfers.

activities.purpose: Return an original RPC outcome for duplicate mutation attempts.
data: tenant and user identifier when supplied
activities.storage: Redis or Postgres; completed-result ttl defaults to 172800 seconds (48 hours).

defaultRetention.limit: Redis key expiry or Postgres expiry plus cleanup interval; clear/purgeUser can remove earlier.

erasure.action: Pass tenant/user metadata, wire the durable store into live.forget, and verify purgeUser completion.
erasure.limitations: Legacy/anonymous/unmapped rows cannot be selected by user and remain until expiry or broader deletion.

hostActions: Reduce TTL if retry semantics permit.
Ensure cached results exclude unnecessary personal data.
Monitor cleanup when using Postgres.
activities.transfer: Redis/Postgres provider and replica/backup regions must be assessed.

activities.purpose: Retain failed webhook deliveries for diagnosis or replay.
activities.storage: In-memory, Redis, or Postgres dead-letter queue; default maximum is 1000 and ttlMs defaults to 0 (no time expiry).

defaultRetention.policy: capacity-bounded but indefinite by time unless ttlMs is configured
defaultRetention.limit: Oldest-record eviction, positive ttlMs, delete/clear, or purgeUser with forgetUserId.

erasure.action: Configure forgetUserId before capture, call purgeUser/live.forget, and verify concurrent-delivery tombstone and durable deletion behavior.
erasure.limitations: Records captured without a user extractor are not selectively purgeable; replaying a record creates a new downstream copy.

hostActions: Set a positive ttlMs.
Restrict operator access and redact failure data.
Treat replay recipients as a new processing event.
activities.transfer: Store provider and webhook destination may be separate processors/recipients and transfers.

activities.purpose: Execute durable background work and scheduled room alarms.
activities.storage: Postgres tasks retain terminal rows for seven days by default; jobs delete completed rows; Redis/Postgres alarms remain until atomically claimed/fired, replaced, cleared, or deleted.

defaultRetention.policy: mixed: task terminal TTL, job completion deletion, and event-bounded alarm lifetime
defaultRetention.limit: Task rowTtl defaults to 604800 seconds; alarms have no independent maximum age and overdue/unresolvable records may persist until recovery or deletion.

erasure.action: Use task forgetUserId/purgeUser; remove or replace affected queued jobs and alarms using application identifiers; verify in-flight handlers and downstream effects separately.
erasure.limitations: Jobs and alarms are not automatically user-indexed; deleting a work row cannot undo external side effects already performed.

hostActions: Minimise payloads and results.
Set task TTL from business need.
Define cancellation/compensation and unresolved-alarm cleanup.
Cover downstream effects in erasure workflows.
activities.transfer: Postgres/Redis providers, workers, and downstream services may be processors/recipients.

activities.purpose: Coordinate presence, groups, cursors, locks, rate limits, and pub/sub across instances.
activities.storage: Process memory and Redis keys/pub-sub with surface-specific TTLs and leave/disconnect cleanup; application selectors can introduce additional personal fields.

defaultRetention.policy: connection, lease, configured TTL, or explicit leave lifecycle
defaultRetention.limit: Disconnect/lease expiry, rate-limit/lock TTL, explicit leave/clear, user purge where supported, or infrastructure deletion.

erasure.action: Disconnect/remove the subject, invoke live.forget for registered state, delete application-defined keys, and wait for or explicitly remove leased Redis state.
erasure.limitations: Pub/sub recipients and application consumers may retain copies; arbitrary selector fields cannot be discovered automatically.

hostActions: Project only public fields.
Keep TTLs finite.
Prohibit raw personal values in metric labels and broad group/topic names.
activities.transfer: Redis provider and every subscribed application instance receive the routed identifiers/events.

activities.purpose: Operate, secure, diagnose, and measure the deployment.
activities.storage: Custom event sink or console, metric scraper/backend, and configured tracing provider/exporter. The ecosystem does not set backend retention.

defaultRetention.policy: host-defined; no ecosystem deletion or retention guarantee after export
defaultRetention.limit: The in-process metric registry is process-lifetime, but external logs, metrics, and spans follow each backend's policy.

erasure.action: Search and delete or irreversibly de-identify records in every sink/provider according to the deployment policy and legal basis.
erasure.limitations: live.forget and store purgeUser do not reach logging, metrics, trace, SIEM, support, or backup systems.

hostActions: Keep topics, user ids, addresses, cookies, tokens, and payloads out of metric labels.
Classify custom attributes.
Set backend retention/access and document any security-log exception.
activities.transfer: Every hosted logging, metric, tracing, SIEM, and support vendor must be evaluated as a recipient/subprocessor and for international transfer.

activities.purpose: Persist application domain state, CRDT documents, exports, analytics, or disaster-recovery copies selected by the deployer.
activities.storage: Application databases, object stores, analytics systems, caches, replicas, and backups outside the ecosystem's automatic inventory.

defaultRetention.limit: No ecosystem default, discovery, or deletion guarantee.

erasure.action: Run application-specific deletion/de-identification across primary, derived, replicated, cached, exported, and backed-up copies and retain non-personal completion evidence.
erasure.limitations: An ecosystem success result cannot attest stores that were never registered or data that cannot be mapped to the subject.

hostActions: Extend the generated RoPA with every application store and recipient.
Document backup deletion/put-beyond-use timing.
Test complete subject mapping.
activities.transfer: All application storage, analytics, backup, support, and recovery providers/regions are deployment-specific.
